title: HelperSSHConnectionsResult
description: Result of the ssh service's connections op: the helper's whole supervisor table, and the subscription that keeps it current (nocx-oalo1.6.2; design §5.10, scenario 7). THE TABLE IS THE HELPER'S, NOT THE ASKING COORDINATOR'S: one helper serves every coordinator of the same user (D12), and this answer carries all of its supervisors to each caller — a restarted coordinator has nothing of its own to rebuild from, and it must not mistake the answer for a list of its own connections. The table is never pruned, so it also includes connections in `ended` and supervisors that never got a link; read each entry's `state` before acting on it. It has to include the connections NO PANE rides: a tunnel, a probe lease, the far helper's own lane. The old per-destination subscription could never show a coordinator those, because nothing had named their destinations on the new connection. The array is never null: an empty table is [], because a decoder distinguishing 'this helper holds nothing' from 'no answer' needs the empty case to arrive as one, and a coordinator that read a missing list as 'nothing' would rebuild nothing and never notice.

connections.description: One entry per supervisor the helper has created, in a stable order (by connection id), so two answers to the same question are the same document. Supervisors are never removed, so the list is every connection this helper has ever named and not only the ones with a live transport: entries in `ended` and entries that never dialled are here too, and the entry's own `state` says which is which.

items.description: One connection: the observation the event stream carries, plus the two facts a restart cannot do without. The observation is the SAME declaration `ssh.connection-state` makes, by $ref and not by a copy, so a receiver folds a list entry and a live event with one function (AD-8).

destination.description: The RESOLVED destination this connection was acquired for, exactly as the op that acquired it carried it. It is what a restarted coordinator redials from, and it cannot be re-derived: the connection id is a digest over the account, the credential principal and the route, and a digest is not a destination. Absent for a connection no destination-naming op ever acquired: a ProxyJump HOP of a route is dialled by the carrier under its own pool key, so it never passes the destination funnel and no destination is recorded for it. (`connection`, `reconnect`, `disconnect` and every pooled acquisition all name one, so a reconnecting or disconnected connection normally does have this.)

hostKeyFingerprint.description: The SHA256 fingerprint of the host key the connection's CURRENT link was verified against. The host's mode and the person's consent are both keyed by it (ADR-0034, ADR-727g63tr), so a coordinator that restarted cannot rebuild an entry without it. Absent while this helper holds no link for the connection: a fingerprint is what a handshake established, and a supervisor that lost its transport must not go on vouching for one.
